references.text: Almost identical wording: 'The Lord is my strength and my song, he has become my salvation.' The same Hebrew expression עָזִּי וְזִמְרָת יָהּ is used.
Isaiah quotes this song: 'Behold, God is my salvation; I will trust and not be afraid. For the Lord is my strength and my song, he has become my salvation.'
Expresses the same trust in the fathers' God: 'In you our ancestors put their trust; they trusted, and you delivered them.'
Same theme of exalting God: 'My strength, to you I will sing, for God is my fortress, my gracious God.' Uses a similar expression עֻזִּי.
Exaltation of the Lord: 'Exalt the Lord our God; worship at his footstool!' The same verb רום (exalt) is used.
Moses' song that praises the name and greatness of the Lord, a parallel to the exaltation of God in Exodus 15:2.
The reference to 'the God of my fathers' (אֱלֹהֵי אָבִי) connects to the revelation of God as the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
Revelation refers to 'the song of Moses' and 'the song of the Lamb,' which praise God's great and wonderful works.
Same confession about God as salvation: 'O Lord my God, my mighty Savior' - expresses a personal relationship with God as deliverer.
Habakkuk uses similar wording: 'The Lord God is my strength' - same theme of God as the source of strength and joy.
Partial allusion: Reuses Moses' confession 'the God of my father... him I will exalt' to connect one's own song of praise with the historical tradition.
Rare term: Uses the unique expression 'you are my song' which directly links Jeremiah's prayer to Moses' song at the Red Sea.
